Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Knight was limited Wednesday after donning a yellow non-contact jersey in practice, but after ditching it one day later, he was able to handle every on-field rep. That's not to say he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires an evaluation from an independent neurologist, but he's likely on the precipice of doing so. Friday's injury report will determine if Knight heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.

Carter opened the season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained during training camp. He was a limited practice participant in Wednesday's session, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Rams.

Wingard has been working through a knee injury for the past month, but he's now dealing with a groin issue that he may have picked up against the Seahawks in Week 9, when he logged 12 tackles (four solo) while playing every single defensive snap. Wingard has two more chances to practice in full and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams. Kitan Crawford and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson would be the top candidates to start next to Budda Baker at safety if Wingard cannot play in Week 10.

The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.
With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.

Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.

Froholdt played all 51 of the Cardinals' offensive snaps during Sunday's game at Seattle, but he may have suffered a concussion somewhere along the way. He'll need to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, which includes getting clearance from an independent neurologist, before he'll be able to return to game action. With Jon Gaines nursing an ankle injury, Arizona could be forced to turn to 2025 sixth-rounder Hayden Conner, who has limited experience, for reps at center.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Daniels was also limited by an Achilles injury during the Thursday of Week 8 prep. He ultimately avoided an injury designation for that game against the Buccaneers and played without limitations in Week 9 against the Bengals as well. The rookie fourth-round pick's availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be clarified on Friday's injury report.

The rookie wideout was injured in the Week 8 loss to the Bucs and missed last Sunday's loss to the Bengals in Spain. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair picked up extra snaps behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson.

Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Hawkins missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, he likely has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to suit up Monday night against the Chargers. If Hawkins can't play, K'Von Wallace should continue to see more snaps.

Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully, and thus avoid an injury designation, prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losing four games in a row.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Kincaid has opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. He has faced plenty of practice limitations throughout the season, but Kincaid has yet to sit out a game. That pattern seems unlikely to change in Week 10 against the Jets.

A rib injury prevented Dawkins from playing against the Vikings on Monday. He has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets. Tylan Grable would likely start at left tackle if Dawkins is unable to play.

Benford injured his wrist in Monday night's win over the Vikings but was able to return to the contest. Across seven starts this season, he has 31 tackles (21 solo) and seven pass breakups on 89 percent of the defensive snaps.

Anderson is dealing with an ankle injury that caused him to miss practice Thursday and Friday. He was able to log a limited session Saturday, but that won't be enough for him to suit up for Monday Night Football. Austin Corbett figures to start at left guard in Anderson's place.

Shavers will remain sidelined for at least one more game as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL. The wide receiver returned to practice in late October, and he could be activated prior to the team's Week 10 matchup with the Jets.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: The Panthers listed Legette as a full participant Wednesday on their estimated practice report. He gets the same listing after an actual practice and seems to be closing in on a return from injured reserve. Carolina would need to activate Legette by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him on the roster for Sunday's game at New Orleans. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver earlier this season, and neither John Metchie nor Brycen Tremayne has made much of an impact in his absence.

The Panthers also listed Brooks as 'FP' on Wednesday's estimated practice report. Now that he's actually logged a full practice, Brooks may have a real shot to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game at New Orleans. The Panthers would need to make that move by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Brooks on the active roster Sunday.

Okereke was estimated as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he remained sidelined for Thursday's full-speed practice. Barring a return to practice Friday, Okereke could be in line for a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Saints after he racked up 49 tackles (31 solo) through his first seven games with the Panthers.

Jackson was placed on injured reserve late in September after suffering a groin injury in Week 3 against Cleveland. The 29-year-old's potential return would greatly help a depleted Carolina secondary, which lost both Jackson and Jaycee Horn (quadriceps) early in the season. Jackson has five tackles (three solo) in his two full regular-season games.

Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.
With Stevenson sidelined and Malik Muhammad (toe) inactive, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips will take on more defensive snaps alongside Jaylon Phillips and Kyler Gordon at cornerback for the Bears.

Muhammad was expected to be able to return to action in Week 9, but the cornerback will now be forced to miss a second straight game while nursing a toe injury he suffered in Week 7. In his absence, Josh Blackwell is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities at cornerback behind starters Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson versus the Buccaneers.

Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.
Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.

Iosivas, who landed on IR on Sept. 26, is bouncing back from surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, and the wideout's looming return to Thursday's practice has him trending the right direction ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers. Once he's back in action, Iosivas will slot back in behind top WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, a role that doesn't typically yield steady volume.

Dugger has been sidelined by a quadriceps injury for the Bengals' last two games, and he has not been cleared to return to practice. He would likely need to practice in at least a limited fashion over the next two days in order to have a realistic chance of playing against the Steelers on Sunday.

Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: The same applies to Fannin's Wednesday practice participation, but it's worth noting that the tight end was also limited by his groin issue last Thursday and Friday before approaching the Browns' Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints without an injury designation. Friday's practice/injury report will reveal whether that pattern is repeated ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Zac Jackson of The Athletic previously reported that Boston indicated that his toe was feeling better and said he was hoping to return to practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session. With Boston now set to log another 'DNP,' what the wideout is able to do (if anything) Friday will be telling with regard to his chances of being available Sunday against the Texans.

Schwesinger may have tweaked his wrist during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he logged a season-high 15 tackles (10 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one forced fumble. He has two more chances to log a full practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Ward was on the field for 73 of the Browns' 75 defensive snaps in Week 9, and his presence at practice Wednesday suggests his injury is likely not severe. If he can log a full practice Thursday or Friday, there's a solid chance he'll be able to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Williams has been working through a hamstring issue as of late, although he was cleared to play against the Saints in Week 9, when he logged seven tackles (five solo) in a 23-22 overtime loss for the Browns. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited session, and he has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Burton suffered a calf injury against the Saints in Week 9. He was cleared to return to that contest, but he's still working through the injury and was held out of Wednesday's practice. Burton will have two more opportunities to practice ahead of Sunday's contest against the Texans.

Hickman suffered a concussion in Week 9 against the Saints. He will have multiple steps to work through, but has the full week to clear concussion protocol. The fourth-year pro has 57 tackles (26 solo), four pass deflections and one interception in nine regular-season games this season.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Mingo didn't practice for a second consecutive day due to foot and ankle issues. He logged a season-high 31 offensive snaps in the narrow win over the Colts in Week 9. Mingo could be busier than usual once again versus the 49ers if KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and George Pickens (hamstring) miss another game. However, Mingo will need to be cleared to suit up for that to happen.

Turpin was limited for a second consecutive practice. He has missed the last three games, and if that trend continues Sunday versus San Francisco, Jonathan Mingo (ankle) and Camden Brown could remain more involved than usual.

As he was a week ago, Pickens continues to operate with practice restrictions, giving him just one more chance this week to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers. He's looking to limit his absence to only one contest due to a hamstring injury.

The Cowboys' top cornerback has appeared in just four games with the team since being acquired from the Steelers ahead of Week 4. He missed last Sunday's win over the Colts, so Cobie Durant made the start opposite DaRon Bland and played all 64 defensive snaps.

The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

Ezeiruaku suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Colts and didn't return. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the 49ers, Ezeiruaku may not be able to suit up for that one. If that's the case, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more snaps.

Locke suffered a concussion in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. While he was cleared to play in Week 9 against the Colts, he suffered another concussion. Now, Locke will miss at least one game, though the team will presumably be overly cautious before allowing him to get back on the field, meaning Markquese Bell may be in line for more snaps.

At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.

Denver Broncos.longComment: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.
Moss has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Jahdae Barron will likely finish the game at outside cornerback for the Broncos.

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Wonnum posted back-to-back full practices Wednesday and Thursday while working through a concussion. It's unclear whether he can play in Sunday's matchup against New England, but he appears to be moving in the right direction. The 29-year-old has 14 tackles (eight solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass deflection across seven regular-season games.

Reed did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a hip injury suffered late in Week 8. Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw could see extended playing time for the second straight week in Reed's stead. Reed has 42 tackles (29 solo) and seven pass deflections, including one interception, in seven regular-season games.

Joseph was a full participant in practice Thursday, but it appears the Lions are taking a cautious approach to his return. The 25-year-old has one more chance to return from the reserve/PUP list in Week 11 before he becomes ineligible for the remainder of the season.

Vaki missed practice for the second straight day due to an ankle injury that occurred in the Lions' Week 9 win over the Dolphins. The 25-year-old will likely need to practice in some capacity Friday for a chance to play in Week 10 against the Patriots in Germany. If Vaki is unavailable Sunday, Jacob Saylors will likely serve as the No. 2 back behind Jahmyr Gibbs against New England.

For a second week in a row, St. Brown is enduring practice restrictions due to a rib injury. Having said that, he still suited up this past Sunday in Miami and earned a 75-percent snap share en route to eight catches (on 10 targets) for 86 yards. Friday's injury report will determine if St. Brown has a designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Patriots in Munich.

Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Franklin has missed the last three games for the Packers. It appears the 30-year-old won't be back on the field in Week 10 versus the Vikings. If that's the case, Isaiah McDuffie remains in line for more snaps.

Moore has been working his way back from an ankle injury after last playing in the Week 5 meeting with the Bears. The wideout remains on injured reserve. While it's unclear if Moore will be ready to suit up Sunday versus the Vikings, it appears his return is imminent.

Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the Week 4 meeting with the Buccaneers and eventually landed on injured reserve. While he's been working his way back since then, it's unknown if he will be ready for Sunday's divisional clash with the Vikings.

Since Williams made his season debut in Week 6 against the Cowboys, his snap share has ranged from 48 to 60 percent over the last four games, and he's made his mark on offense in each one, gathering in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and one touchdown and taking eight carries for 44 yards. A groin issue has capped his reps so far this week, and Friday's injury report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Vikings.

Despite dealing with an illness Wednesday, Parsons was able to go down as a limited participant in the ensuing jog-through, and he maintained that activity level one day later. He's seeking his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee, and he so far has completed nearly two weeks of capped sessions since he was designated for return from the reserve/PUP list last Wednesday. Friday's injury report will reveal if Parsons has a chance to play Sunday against the Vikings, but more realistically the Packers likely are eyeing a road matchup with the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25 for his season debut.

Whyle faces an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol before Sunday's game against the Vikings. If he's unable to do so, he would sit out for a second consecutive game while Mark Redman and Jonnu Smith continue to function as the depth options behind Tucker Kraft.

Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and is in line to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are currently available to handle Green Bay's backfield duties while Jacobs is sidelined, plus Chris Brooks (ankle) is a candidate to return from IR as soon as this weekend.

Hopper picked up a chest injury during the first quarter of the Packers' win against the Patriots in Week 9 and did not return. The good news for the third-year pro is that he was cleared to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday. If Hopper can upgrade his participation over the next two days, then he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Vikings.

Bullard may have tweaked his ankle during the Packers' win over the Patriots in Week 9, when he logged three tackles (two solo). He'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, but if he cannot play in that contest, then Kamal Hadden, Carrington Valentine and Benjamin St-Juste would all be in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary.

The Packers hosted a jog-through practice Wednesday, but Van Ness was a spectator for that session due to a back injury that he may have picked up during the Packers' Week 9 win over the Patriots, when he logged one solo tackle. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's NFC North tilt against Minnesota.

Houston Texans.longComment: Blankenship has missed the Texans' last two games. While he's still not guaranteed to suit up in Week 10 versus the Browns, he appears to be moving in a favorable direction. If Blankenship remains sidelined Sunday, M.J. Stewart would presumably draw another start.

This is the first mention of Hunter's hamstring injury. His availability for Friday's practice should provide more clarity regarding his status for Sunday's game against the Browns, though he should be considered questionable for now. The 32-year-old has appeared in all eight of the Texans' regular-season games, accumulating 10 total tackles (nine solo) and 4.0 sacks.

Anderson popped up on the injury report due to an ankle injury, though he will have another opportunity to log a full session Friday. For now, he should at least be considered questionable for Week 10 against Cleveland. The 25-year-old has appeared in all eight regular-season games for the Texans, garnering 35 total tackles (19 solo), 9.5 sacks and one forced fumble.

Harrison  was limited Wednesday, so the WR's downgrade in participation a day later clouds his status for Sunday's game against the Browns. In three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has combined to catch six of his 11 targets for 60 yards and a TD in in that span.

Marks was limited Wednesday, so his 'DNP' on Thursday is concerning, though it could be more of a workload management situation, as opposed to a setback-related downgrade, a notion supported by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston's report that the running back dealt with mild knee discomfort in Wednesday's practice and didn't finish the session for precautionary reasons. Meanwhile, fellow backfield member David Montgomery (groin) -- who hasn't played since Week 5 -- returned to a limited session Thursday. Valuable context regarding the duo's status will arrive Friday, when the Texans have their final practice before Sunday's road game against the Browns.

Montgomery, who last saw game action in Week 5, was listed as a 'DNP' on Wednesday, with his upgrade to limited participation a day later especially notable given that fellow RB Woody Marks (knee) didn't practice. Friday's injury report will reveal both the practice participation, as well as the duo's official game statuses' for Sunday's road contest against the Browns.

Al-Shaair played through a groin injury in Week 9, and it's unclear whether that or his personal issue is the driving force behind his pair of practice absences to begin Week 10 prep. The starting  linebacker has one more chance to resume practicing Firday before the Texans face the Browns on Sunday.

Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Hummel was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and it was encouraging to see him back on the field after recovering from groin surgery. The Texans face the Browns on Sunday, but Hummel would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for that contest.

Jordan has dealt with knee and foot injuries this season and has played pretty sparingly behind Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau and Cade Stover for much of the campaign. Jordan has logged just 29 offensive snaps across nine appearances.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: The veteran linebacker didn't practice at all last week and missed the Week 9 loss to the Cowboys. CJ Allen played every defensive snap in Davis-Gaither's absence and would be in line for a similar role Sunday against Miami if the latter is unable to play.

The veteran blocking tight end was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Cowboys. If he can't play Sunday against Miami, Will Mallory, Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown would be next in line for snaps at tight end behind Tyler Warren.

Key hasn't played since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Commanders. Now, after five weeks, the 30-year-old may begin practicing. He will likely need to string together multiple positive practices for a chance to play in Week 10.

"We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.
Travis is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the knee injury he sustained during Sunday's loss to Dallas. In his absence, Luke Tentua will likely take over as Indianapolis' starting right tackle.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Walker opened the week as a non-participant in practice Wednesday due to a rib injury that he played through in Week 9. Practice participation in some form Friday could improve his chances of playing in Week 10. The 25-year-old has 21 tackles (nine solo), including 3.0 sacks, and one pass deflection in eight regular-season games.

Meyers has managed one injury or another throughout the season without missing any games. His return to practice Thursday after a Wednesday absence suggests this may just be another cause of maintenance/caution. If Meyers plays, he'll face a Tennessee defense that's allowing a league 40.7 PPR points per game to wide receivers.

The catch is that Tuten didn't practice last week and ended up playing in a 33-10 win at Baltimore on Thursday night. Rodriguez played through his hand injury, so he should be able to take on an expanded workload this week if Tuten doesn't play.

Tuten didn't practice Wednesday either, though as Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville points out, Tuten logged 'DNPs' Monday through Wednesday last week yet still played in last Thursday's win over the Ravens. In any case, Friday's practice report will reveal whether Tuten is able to work at all this week, as well as his game status for Sunday's game against the Titans. Next up for carries if he ends up sidelined this weekend is Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was limited Thursday.

Green landed on injured reserve in mid-September after suffering an elbow injury in Week 1 against the Browns. The Jaguars now have 21 days to activate Green from injured reserve, otherwise the Colorado product would be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Moore suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Jets. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the Falcons, there's certainly the possibility of an absence. If that's the case, Joshua Ezeudu may fill the void at right tackle.

Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Zuhn entered the league's concussion protocol during the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. He'll need to clear protocol in order to play against the Seahawks on Sunday, otherwise Caleb Rogers would likely serve as the Raiders' starting right guard.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders. It appears he will remain on the shelf for Monday's game versus the Ravens unless he shows signs of progress in the next few days.

Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.

With teammate Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back injury in Week 9, Harris played 59 of the Chargers' 68 offensive snaps, drawing a team-high seven targets. It seems like he may have picked up an injury of his own along the way though, which makes his availability for Week 10 worth monitoring. He'll have two more chances to manage a full practice before the Chargers publish their last injury report of the week Saturday.

In this past Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Mitchell carried seven times for 33 yards and caught three of his four targets for 34 yards, while losing a fumble.The 24-year-old, who is currently operating in a backfield time share with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal in his first campaign with the Chargers, now has two more chances to upgrade his practice participation level ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com relayed Monday that Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh viewed McConkey as "day to day" with the back spasms that led to the wideout not logging any snaps in this past Sunday's loss to the Texans. With a 'DNP' on the record for Thursday, McConkey now has two more chances to practice ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Allen popped up on the Rams' injury report Wednesday with an oblique issue, and now his availability for Week 10 appears to be in serious jeopardy. With teammates Tyler Higbee (illness), Colby Parkinson (ribs) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) also dealing with health concerns, rookie second-rounder Max Klare currently seems to be the only Rams tight end who is a lock to suit up for Sunday's game at Arizona.

With this transaction officially in the books, Nacua will be required to miss at least the next four games due to the PCL and MCL sprains and turf-toe injury that he sustained near the end of this past Sunday's win at Washington. During the initial stage of Nacua's absence, the Rams will lean on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wide receiver until Davante Adams (hamstring) is ready to return from injured reserve.

While Parkinson continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps due to the rib issue that sidelined him in Week 8 against the Chargers, fellow TE Tyler Higbee showed up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness, and reserve option Davis Allen went from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later. Friday's practice report will unveil the odds of each player to suit up Sunday at Arizona.

With Higbee's addition to the Rams' Week 10 injury report Thursday, the team's top three tight ends on the active roster are dealing with health concerns, as Colby Parkinson has been limited by a rib injury, while Davis Allen downgraded from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later due to an oblique issue. As a result, Friday's practice report will be telling for who among the trio may be available Sunday in Arizona.

The Rams are managing Garrett's practice reps after he returned from a seven-game absence this past Sunday at Washington, when he posted 3.0 sacks of Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if Garrett has a designation for Sunday's contest at Arizona.

It was the second consecutive DNP for Curl, who is now battling a toe injury after nearly missing the Week 9 meeting with Washington due to a foot issue. The 27-year-old might carry an injury designation heading into Week 10 against the Cardinals, but if he isn't out there, Jaylen McCollough is a candidate to replace him in the starting lineup.

McDuffie has been sidelined for three of the Rams' last four games with a back injury, preventing him from suiting up for Week 9 against the Commanders. He would need to log at least a limited practice over the next two days in order to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the Cardinals.

In that scenario, Adams could back in action as soon as Week 12 following the Rams' bye week. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is destined to miss multiple weeks, which, for the time being leaves Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Danielsand Xavier Smith as the healthy WRs on the team's active roster.

This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

McVay said part of the decision whether to place Avila on IR will be influenced by concerns that the team could use up all of its eight injured-reserve slots for players eligible to return later in the season. Either way, for as long as Avila remains sidelined, 2024 sixth rounder Beaux Limmer projects to fill in at left guard.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Bell was listed as limited Wednesday, so his apparent downgrade in participation a day later puts the focus on what the wideout is able to do Friday as it relates to his status for Sunday's game against the Colts. Through eight contests overall, Bell has 12 catches for 148 yards and no TDs on 27 targets, and he's coming off a zero-catch effort in the Dolphins' Week 9 loss to the Lions, during which the 2026 third-rounder was on the field for 63 percent of his team's snaps on offense.

Baker has been on Miami's PUP list since August, but it looks like he's making progress toward returning to game action soon. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which the Dolphins can activate him before they'd be required to keep him inactive for the rest of the campaign.

The rookie tight end previously dealt with a hamstring injury before injuring his quad in last Sunday's loss to the Lions. A block-first tight end, Kacmarek has four catches for 30 yards on nine targets across eight games this season.

With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Cashman was injured in the Week 9 meeting with the Bills. He missed practice for a second consecutive day, so his chances of suiting up in Week 10 against the Packers don't appear to be high. If Cashman is ruled out for that contest, Ivan Pace could see more snaps.

Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

Wentz had his left ankle stepped on by Vikings left guard Joe Huber during Monday's loss to the Bills, and while he didn't miss a snap before Max Brosmer took over for the final possession, the former has operated with practice restrictions to begin Week 10 prep. With the acquisition of Kirk Cousins on Tuesday and Kyler Murray still week to week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Wentz is expected to return to a reserve role Sunday at Green Bay, but head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't announced a starter for that contest as of Thursday.

Hockenson now has logged back-to-back DNPs to begin Week 10 prep as he tends to wrist and chest injuries. The Vikings may make a ruling on the tight end's status as soon as they post their final practice report of the week Friday, but if Hockenson is inhibited to sidelined Sunday at Green Bay, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew are the next players up at the position.

Murray already has missed one game due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain and is expected to be sidelined longer as the Vikings begin prep for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, but O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to him as the team's Week 10 starting QB as of Wednesday. Assuming Murray is out again this weekend, Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer will be the signal-caller options at O'Connell's disposal.
Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

New England Patriots.longComment: Henry played through the injury in last week's loss to Green Bay and has now managed back-to-back limited practices to open Week 10. He'll likely gut it out again Sunday against the Lions in Munich, and while the matchup is favorable, rookie Eli Raridon had been cutting into Henry's snaps and targets even before the veteran injured his foot in a Week 8 win at Miami. Henry played 49.2 percent of snaps in the Week 9 loss to Green Bay, catching each of his three targets for 35 yards.

Stevenson's participation may come as a surprise after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that the running back was likely to miss a few weeks. The Patriots have a Week 11 bye, but first they'll face the Lions in Munich this Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET. Corey Kiner is next up as New England's lead runner if Stevenson doesn't play. Patriots wideout DeMario Douglas told reporters that Stevenson hopes to play, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

Brown has been listed as limited on consecutive days to open the Patriots' Week 10 prep in Munich. He would likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying a questionable tag into Sunday's game against the Lions, which kicks off at 9:30 a.m. EST. In three appearances for New England, Brown has nine catches for 101 yards.

Woods was unable to play against the Packers in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited practice, and if he's cleared to play Sunday against the Lions in Munich, then he would be a candidate for more work in the secondary due to the absence of Carlton Davis (knee).

Brown tweaked his knee against the Packers in Week 9, and the injury is severe enough for him to not travel with the team to Munich. In his absence, Walter Rouse is expected to serve as the Patriots' starter at left guard. Since the Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, Brown's next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Byard was working through a chest injury in October, but it's unclear whether he's dealing with the same issue for the start of Week 10 prep. The veteran safety will have two more chances to increase his practice participation before the Patriots travel to Munich to face the Lions on Sunday. Byard has 43 tackles (23 solo) and three pass defenses (including one interception) through the first nine games of the regular season.

Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Henderson was one of three players listed as out for this weekend's contest, signaling that they are not in line to make the trip to Germany. With Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) not practicing Wednesday and reportedly on track to miss some time, it looks like Corey Kiner is trending toward leading New England's Week 10 backfield, with Lan Larison also in the mix and Terrell Jennings a potential practice-squad elevation. New England has a bye in Week 11, so Nov. 29 against the Chargers is Henderson's soonest possible return date.
The fullback hasn't played since Week 4. He's logged 58 snaps on offense and another 39 on special teams across four appearances this season.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Donaldson has yet to resume practicing since sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 7, which suggests he's trending for another absence in Sunday's Week 10 matchup with the Panthers. Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are both expected to be available, while Travis Etienne's (hamstring) status is up in the air as the latter tries to work his way back from a hamstring injury that landed him on IR.

The Saints designated Etienne for return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he so far has logged back-to-back limited practices during Week 10 prep. He'll have one more opportunity Friday to put himself in a position for his first game action since Week 3, when he suffered a strained left hamstring.

Per Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio New Orleans, Moore also said Monday that McCoy is not tending to a long-term or season-ending injury, and he does not believe it will require surgery. William Sherman filled in for McCoy at center after he exited during the fourth quarter in Week 9, but Cesar Ruiz also has experience at the position, and rookie fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright is available should the Saints need him at guard.

New York Giants.longComment: Harrison was limited at practice throughout the week and has since been ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with the Commanders. The 28-year-old has played sparingly on defense during the 2026 campaign, though his absence will be felt on special teams. Harrison's next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 11 versus Jacksonville.

New York Jets.longComment: Wilson was limited in a second consecutive practice Thursday, though he took a step in the right direction, as Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports that Wilson shed the red non-contact jersey at Thursday's practice. If Wilson can practice without limitations Friday, that would go a long way in his quest to clear concussion protocol in time to face the Bills on Sunday.

Cooper officially goes down as a limited participant for a second consecutive practice, matching the participation level of Garrett Wilson (concussion). Since returning from an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve, Cooper has 19 catches for 276 yards and two touchdowns in four games, even with a zero-catch Week 8 performance during that stretch.

The Jets only held a walkthrough practice Wednesday, and they projected that Phillips would not have been able to practice at all if a standard session had taken place. He'll likely need to get back on the practice field in a full capacity Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Wright was out in Week 9 because of his back injury, and his status for Week 10 is now up in the air as well. He'll probably need to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Ossai has missed the Jets' last four games while recovering from an ankle injury. He's been able to practice in a limited capacity, but he may need to log a full session in order to be cleared to play against the Bills on Sunday.
The linebacker missed last Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and has been strictly limited to special teams this season, playing 106 snaps in kick coverage.

Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

In a corresponding transaction, the Jets signed tackle Blake Freeland to their active roster. Mitchell, who has not made a start on the offensive line yet this season, will now have to miss at least the next four games.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

Harmon said he's 100 percent healthy, but the team will take things day-to-day with the defensive lineman, according to Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com. Harmon hasn't played since Week 4. He's recorded 12 tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks, across 85 defensive snaps this season.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Greenlaw had eight tackles in Sunday's win over the Raiders. While he was limited Thursday, he has more time to get cleared to suit up versus the Cowboys in Week 10. If Greenlaw can't get on the field, Jaden Dugger and Garret Wallow are both in line for more snaps.

Shanahan's comments signal the 49ers are taking an extra cautious approach with the veteran wideout in the hopes that he'll be available down the home stretch of the season. While Evans hasn't officially been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, he isn't expected to suit up in Week 10, per Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site. Until he's fully recovered and ready to go again, his absence should continue to open up additional opportunities outside for 2025 fourth-rounder Jordan Watkins.

Samuel has managed back-to-back capped sessions to kick off Week 10 prep as he vies for his first game action since Week 5 at Seattle, when he injured his right hamstring. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday in Dallas.

The 49ers opened West's 21-day practice window Wednesday, and he was limited in his return to on-field practice. He landed on injured reserve in late September due to a knee injury, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys.

Lenoir is considered day-to-day due to a foot injury that he picked up in Week 9 against the Raiders. He was an observer for Wednesday's session, and he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's tilt against the Cowboys. Lenoir has accumulated 33 tackles (20 solo) and one pass defense through eight regular-season games.

Green injured his back in the second half of the 49ers' win over the Raiders in Week 9, and he finished that game with four tackles (two solo) and one interception. Per Barrows, head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated Monday that Green is considered day-to-day, so the third-year defensive back's practice participation over the next two days will determine whether he'll be available for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season. The fourth-round rookie finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 15 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, a defensed pass, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery (which he returned for a touchdown) over eight contests. San Francisco's recent acquisition of DeForest Buckner softens the blow of losing Halton a bit.

In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Lock continues to deal with a right elbow injury, and he's also tending to an oblique issue that he suffered this past Sunday against the Cardinals. He discussed the new health concern Thursday, telling Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle that he's "feeling good" and the oblique injury is on his backside, which is easier to deal with than if it was on the lead side. Lock so far has had his practice reps capped this week as a result, and Friday's injury report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas.

Hall only played 29 of the Seahawks' 53 defensive snaps in Week 9 versus the Cardinals, and the fact that he's dealing with a back injury might be part of the reason why. He'll probably have to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Williams was sidelined for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals due to a shoulder injury, and now his status for Week 10 is in question. He'll likely need to return to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to put himself on track to play Sunday at Las Vegas.

Nelson is currently considered week-to-week, although head coach Mike Macdonald said the team isn't planning to place Nelson on injured reserve. The 2018 first-round pick will likely target the Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco to make his return, and Grey Zabel will likely start at left guard in his absence.

Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Winfield sustained an ankle injury late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. With Winfield unavailable, Ifeatu Melifonwu will continue to operate as one of Tampa Bay's primary safeties versus Chicago.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Spears worked out on a side field for at least part of Thursday's practice, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com, which is a step in the right direction after Spears didn't practice Wednesday. Tony Pollard (finger/rest) didn't practice Thursday, but with Tennessee's coaching staff suggesting that rookie Nicholas Singleton could start to get more involved moving forward, Spears is unlikely to handle more than a handful of touches even if the latter gets the green light for his first action since Week 6.

Since rest is included among the reasons Pollard didn't practice Thursday, he's likely to resume practicing in at least some capacity Friday. After staying put at the trade deadline, Pollard is poised to retain the lead role in Tennessee's backfield for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Pollard compiled 292 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns across Tennessee's last two games prior to a Week 9 bye.

Turron Davenport of ESPN.com previously noted that Tate was able to work on the side with the Titans' training staff during Thursday's session, but in the end he was officially listed as a 'DNP' for the second consecutive day. Friday's practice will thus loom large in terms of Tate's potential availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Next up for added WR snaps this weekend in the event that Tate remains sidelined is Chimere Dike, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley.

Barton has started all eight games at linebacker this season, but his snaps have been dialed back some in recent weeks. He and Cedric Gray are part-time linebackers behind every-down middle linebacker Anthony Hill (neck), who also missed practice Wednesday.

Hill appears to have been injured at the tail end of the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals, as he played just 96 percent of the defensive snaps after not missing a single snap in any of the first seven games of the season. With Cody Barton (concussion) also a DNP on Wednesday, the Titans could be down a couple of key linebackers for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.

In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.
With Skoronski sidelined, Garrett Dellinger is now in the game at left guard.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Patrick suffered a concussion during Sunday's game versus the Rams, and it will keep him out for his third game this season in Week 10. In his absence, rookie sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin figures to take over at center Thursday.

Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not presumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Payne will be out long-term with a foot injury suffered in practice. With both Javon Kinlaw (knee) and Payne out, Tim Settle will have a larger role at nose tackle going forward.
